name: board-flow
description: Adds a single atlassian-expert worker plus Jira-aware slash commands (configure, capture, plan-track-build-validate, execute, fix, drain, triage, prove, prove-drain, decide, advance) on top of any topology that ships planning-lead, engineering-lead, and validation-lead subagents — or any topology with a custom lifecycle declared in board-flow.yaml (project root, used by /advance). /execute auto-routes Bug cards to /fix (reproduce-fix-verify); use --force-feature-flow to override. /triage grooms the backlog — classifies each card (already-implemented → In Review, ready → To Do, obsolete → Won't Do, needs-decision → grills you) by inspecting the codebase + git for evidence, writing nothing until you confirm; it also persists the execution ORDER and the `why` behind each position into .claude/programs/<project_key>/plan.yaml (schema common/plan-schema.yaml, mode: single-track), merged never overwritten, because Jira stores the queue and neither the order nor its rationale — which used to die in the chat that produced them. Reading that plan is /common:next (it lives in common because a plan does not require a tracker); board-flow contributes the half only it can do — reconciling the plan against the live board before it answers. /execute, /fix and /prove close with "And now?": the card's Human validation route verbatim (already mandatory via summary-nulls-gate, never before aggregated) plus the next unblocked item of the plan — so the end of a card stops leaving "validate it by hand" and "pull the next card" competing in silence. /prove + /prove-drain run the change-driven proof gate (via the topology's proof-reviewer) to triage the Review column by evidence; /prove-drain closes cards together only when they are causally coupled AND share one validation boundary, and even then requires per-card evidence, reason and debt impact (independent risk or debt forbids joint closure) — a batch-level "all proven, same fix" is the absence of evidence formatted as a conclusion. /decide picks up where the proof gate stops: it reads the cards sitting in Review NOW, takes each one's proof artifact (.claude/proof/<KEY>.yaml), classifies why it stopped at NEEDS-HUMAN into the seven named reasons (docs/needs-human-motivos.md), drops the ones that are nobody's decision (Docker absent, tool missing), groups the rest by reason and asks ONE question per group with a recommendation — answered in batch ("1 yes, 2 no") and applied. It proves nothing itself; /prove and /prove-drain are what prove, and /prove-drain now ends by handing its held set to /decide. Human waivers live in .claude/waivers. /drain names an outcome terminal for every attempted card (SHIPPED / BLOCKED / DEFERRED / DROPPED / ERROR); "needs attention" is not a state, and the drain is unfinished while attempted-count exceeds named-outcome-count. Scope the *-drain sweeps to a board slice via a raw-JQL scope block in board-flow.yaml (per-command and per-topology overrides, plus --scope/--no-scope per run); single-card commands warn when a named card is out of scope. Run /board-flow:configure once after install to set site/project/board. Tested with build-hex, build-team, and discovery. Won't work with build-solo for the lead-based commands. /drain e /prove-drain reservam cada card no board antes de trabalhá-lo (comentário `🔒 claim:` com id por run, relido card a card, expira em 90 min, liberado com `🔓` quando o card termina sem veredito): a listagem de uma coluna é uma foto, e duas sessões paralelas já provaram os mesmos cards por confiar nela — card fora da coluna ou já reservado vira SKIPPED e não consome --max.
